answer: A verifiable delay function (VDF) bound to each agent's public key resists Sybils: before trading, an identity must finish a sequential puzzle taking ten minutes of single-thread work, unparallelizable by adding cores. An attacker wanting a thousand Sybils faces a thousand sequential delays, so cost grows linearly; an honest agent pays once. Even at the nadir of activity it holds, tied to the epoch seed, not peers. Identities enter only through this narrow inlet, one at a time, and each completed VDF is stamped saffron in the public log, so duplicates are spotted at once.
